message.content:
**Answer:**  
Lions (*Panthera leo*) and zebras (*Equus quagga*) do not share a recent common ancestor; they belong to two distinct mammalian orders—Carnivora for lions and Perissodactyla for zebras. Their most recent common ancestor lies deep in the evolutionary tree of placental mammals, dating back roughly 70–80 million years ago, when the lineages that would become modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates were still part of a single, diverse group of early mammals. In other words, while all living mammals share a common ancestor, lions and zebras diverged long before the split between their respective orders.
